report_name: Windows Hello Flaw Allows Persistent Entra ID Access

attack_patterns.name: Native API
attack_patterns.description: Malware with user-level privileges programmatically calls Windows APIs to generate an assertion using the hardware-bound Windows Hello for Business key stored in the TPM, without requiring user interaction, a PIN, or biometrics.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The generated assertion from the WHfB key is used to request and obtain a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) from Microsoft Entra ID, effectively stealing a long-lived token that grants access to the user's cloud resources.

attack_patterns.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
attack_patterns.description: The stolen Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is used as alternate authentication material to silently acquire access tokens for various cloud services (Office 365, Azure) linked to the user's Entra ID account, enabling persistent access.

tools.name: ROADtools
tools.description: A collection of tools for interacting with Microsoft Entra ID. The repository contains the proof-of-concept scripts `fido_assertion.ps1` and `hellopoc.ps1` that demonstrate the Windows Hello for Business abuse.

vulnerabilities.name: Windows Hello for Business PRT Token Abuse
vulnerabilities.description: A design weakness in Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) allows malware running with user-level privileges to programmatically use the hardware-bound WHfB key to obtain a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) from Microsoft Entra ID. This bypasses the need for a PIN, biometrics, or admin rights, challenging the security model of hardware-bound credentials.

identities.name: Dirk-jan Mollema
identities.description: Security researcher who discovered and publicly disclosed the design weakness in Windows Hello for Business.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Vendor of Windows Hello for Business and Microsoft Entra ID. The company reportedly acknowledged the behavior as part of the current design and has not issued a CVE.

identities.name: Organizations using Windows Hello for Business
identities.description: Class of organizations affected by the design weakness that allows for Entra ID persistence from a compromised endpoint using Windows Hello for Business for authentication.

indicators.name: ROADtools WHfB PoC Script Files
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: ROADtools WHfB PoC Script File Creation
id: 4f5b6c7d-8e9f-4a1b-2c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of proof-of-concept script files associated with the ROADtools WHfB abuse technique.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/malware-can-abuse-windows-hello-for.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1528
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\fido_assertion.ps1'
      - '\hellopoc.ps1'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the PoC script files `fido_assertion.ps1` and `hellopoc.ps1` on an endpoint.

indicators.name: ROADtools WHfB PoC Script Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: ROADtools WHfB PoC Script Execution
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of PowerShell scripts associated with the ROADtools WHfB abuse technique.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/malware-can-abuse-windows-hello-for.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1528
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'fido_assertion.ps1'
      - 'hellopoc.ps1'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the command-line execution of the PoC scripts `fido_assertion.ps1` and `hellopoc.ps1` used to abuse WHfB.

indicators.name: Anomalous WHfB Sign-in Without Device ID
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous WHfB Sign-in Without Device ID
id: 6f7a8b9c-0d1e-4f2a-3b4c-5d6e7f8a9b0c
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Entra ID sign-in events using Windows Hello for Business that have an empty or null device ID, which can indicate programmatic token generation by malware.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/malware-can-abuse-windows-hello-for.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1528
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate sessions from incognito browsers or non-SSO browser sessions.
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    AuthenticationDetails|contains: 'WindowsHelloForBusiness'
    DeviceId: null
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a hunting hint provided by the researcher: WHfB sign-in events in Entra ID that have an empty or null device ID, which may indicate programmatic PRT acquisition.
